claim: For an arbitrary probability density g on R^3, the universal cap sup_line integral_line g <= 2 is enough by itself to uniformly bound the pushforward density of q(y)=y1^2+y2^2-y3^2 on the two-sheet/minority-sign levels.
counterexample: For 0<delta<=1/10, a logarithmically extended thin band around q=-1 with density proportional to 1/(sqrt(delta)*y3) has uniformly bounded X-ray norm but q-pushforward density 1/(2delta) on an interval of width 2delta. Mixing one fifth of this shell with a remote cube probability density yields X-ray norm <2 while the q-density is 1/(10delta) near -1.
scope_warning: This is not a counterexample to QFORM-DENSITY: the constructed three-dimensional density is not claimed to be an orthogonal projection of a coordinate-product law. It refutes only the information-loss step that retains probability normalization and the two-dimensional-marginal/X-ray cap while discarding further product-projection structure.
safe_replacement: QFORM-PRODUCT-PROJECTION-TWOSHEET-TRACE-v1: prove the two-sheet trace bound for actual three-dimensional orthogonal marginals of product densities using product provenance and distributed Pluecker data before information loss.
